newsitem.title: USA: Ticket UPS drivers, Houston police union urges.
newsitem.headline: Ticket UPS drivers, Houston police union urges.

text.p: Houston's police union urged local officers on Thursday to ticket United Parcel Service drivers for the slightest infractions to show support for the Teamsters strike of the package carrier.
Houston Police Patrolmen's Union President Terry Martin said he believed most replacement drivers operating UPS trucks during the strike were inexperienced and lacked commercial drivers' licenses.
"We as union members should go into a 'zero tolerance' mode, and do everything possible to get that UPS 'scab' truck off the road," Martin said in a letter to the city's 1,100 union police officers.
A Houston police spokesman declined comment on the union directive, which was faxed on Wednesday to police precincts citywide.
"Chief (Clarence) Bradford is reviewing the situation," he said.
Martin said a crackdown on the replacement UPS drivers would earn the police union support from the trucking union during contract negotiations with the city.

Negotiators from the Teamsters and UPS were heading to the bargaining table for the first time in four days on Thursday to resume talks on ending a national walkout that has crippled the giant parcel delivery company.
